title: Is AI Spending Slowing? NVIDIA Earnings Preview After the SemiAnalysis Cut
creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
summary: Jose Najarro previews Nvidia's Tuesday 17 November earnings, the first since CEO Jensen Huang resigned on 11 November. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO (still also CFO) and the board probe continues. Nvidia is down roughly 35% from its October high (about $239 on 6 October, around $156 at recording) and Wall Street's average price target has fallen from about $328 to about $235 in a week. His eight things to watch: whether the roughly 70% fiscal-2028 revenue-growth guide holds, the Q4 revenue guide (about $123B expected), gross margins staying in the low 70s, any lost confidence from Kress wearing both hats, new export licensing rules for advanced AI chips, cracks in AI spending, Vera Rubin supply, and China. He explains SemiAnalysis's reported AI chip spending cut (2027 forecast from about $770B to $627B) as a cut, not a decline: the new forecast still grows about 60% in 2027 and 21% in 2028, flattening only in 2029. The report is secondhand (paywalled), ignored the CEO change, and Nvidia takes about 66% of the cut. On whether AI spending is slowing, he gives both sides: every hyperscaler pointed to higher 2027 spending, while Microsoft's calendar-2026 capex is about $170B after delays and neoclouds trimmed outlooks on capacity delays. He calls the wider AI industry still bullish, naming Broadcom, AMD, Marvell and memory, but Nvidia itself is the question mark. His call is HOLD on NVDA: he is not selling and is doing nothing until earnings give more information.

calls.thesis: Holding, not selling, ahead of Tuesday 17 Nov earnings: Nvidia is down ~35% from its October high (~$239 on 6 Oct, now ~$156) after Jensen Huang's resignation, and he is doing nothing until the call gives more information. Key watch: whether management holds the ~70% FY2028 revenue-growth guide, Q4 revenue guide (~$123B expected) and low-70s gross margins, plus any impact from new export licensing rules. He still calls the wider AI industry bullish (hyperscalers keep spending) but says Nvidia itself is the question mark.
calls.price_at_call: ~$156 now; ~$239 close on 6 Oct, down ~35% from October high
calls.base_case: Watch and wait: hold the existing position, no buying or selling before earnings; reassess on the 17 Nov call, the 70% FY2028 guide, Q4 guide and margins.
calls.bull_case: Management holds or raises the 70% FY2028 guide (even to 75-80%), Q4 guide and margins intact; SemiAnalysis cut is still growth (2027 AI chip spend $627B, +60% YoY) and hyperscaler capex keeps rising, so the fear is overdone.
calls.bear_case: Guidance trimmed, margins slip further, or new export rules (licenses for advanced AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Brazil) hit guidance; leadership uncertainty and any slip-up on the call feed the 'Nvidia was just Jensen' thesis.
